page: Microsoft Azure D48_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering a balanced core-to-memory ratio across a substantial resource footprint. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor running at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core, 35 MB of L3 cache, and 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation (4.0 GB per core). This configuration contains no local storage and does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid throughput across multi-threaded computational workloads alongside robust memory bandwidth. The processor instruction set supports AVX-512 (including AVX512F and AVX-512 VNNI), AES, and standard vector instructions, delivering 44,706.09 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 38,358.2 in PassMark CPU evaluations. While single-thread speed scores lower relative to high-frequency specialty instances, large-block uncached memory operations register in the top 25% of cloud servers, reaching 189.04 GB/sec for reads and 92.68 GB/sec for writes.

Hardware limitations emerge primarily in tasks dependent on single-threaded execution or hardware acceleration. In language model benchmarks, text generation speeds fall into the lower percentile tiers due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. Furthermore, because local storage is absent, all persistent data and scratch space must be attached via network-based block storage, introducing dependency on network-attached disk tiers.

Qualitatively, the D48_v4 delivers efficient compute and memory density for horizontally scaled operations that consume symmetric resource allocations. The instance fits enterprise application hosting, relational and in-memory database deployments, static web serving infrastructure, Clang compile pipelines, and multi-threaded ETL jobs where expansive memory bandwidth and 48 vCPUs can be utilized concurrently.
description: Microsoft Azure D48_v4 is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores, 192.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), and 35 MB of L3 cache, with no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place its multi-core compute and data-handling abilities in the mid-tier range, while uncached memory bandwidth ranks in the top tier at 189.04 GB/sec for reads and 92.68 GB/sec for writes. However, single-core metrics and unaccelerated LLM text generation yield modest throughput. Relying entirely on remote storage, this server delivers balanced compute and memory density for enterprise web serving, compilation pipelines, in-memory caching systems, and database workloads requiring predictable multi-threaded CPU and high memory throughput.
